findings.evidence: Basic.lean:150 `def IsCollinearSafe`; Basic.lean:207 `theorem isInfraredSafe_iff ... := Iff.rfl`; Counterexamples.lean:79 uses `isInfraredSafe_iff.1 h 0` and Counterexamples.lean:70 uses `h.apply_splitCollinear`, confirming the author treats the bodies as opaque downstream.
findings.fix: Add the mirror lemma: `theorem isCollinearSafe_iff {O : Multiset V → X} : IsCollinearSafe O ↔ ∀ s : Multiset V, ∀ p ∈ s, ∀ z ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, O (splitCollinear p z s) = O s := (Iff.rfl)`.
findings.issue: `IsCollinearSafe` is a `def` whose body is not exposed (no `@[expose]`, per the repo's `public section` convention), and the file supplies only `isCollinearSafe_iff_cons` plus the `apply_*` eliminators. There is no restatement of the definition itself, so downstream a user who has `O (splitCollinear p z s) = O s` for every member `p` cannot introduce `IsCollinearSafe O` without detouring through the `cons` form; `IsInfraredSafe` has exactly this lemma (`isInfraredSafe_iff`, line 207).

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:322-327 are the only declarations about `invariantMassSq` besides the two safety theorems; roadmap README §0.1: "the invariant mass squared as `g (totalMomentum s) (totalMomentum s)`, and prove that both are additive under multiset union".
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem invariantMassSq_zero (g) : invariantMassSq g 0 = 0` and the bilinear union expansion `invariantMassSq g (s + t) = invariantMassSq g s + g s.sum t.sum + g t.sum s.sum + invariantMassSq g t` (note it is *not* additive; the cross terms are the content).
findings.issue: `invariantMassSq` carries only `invariantMassSq_def`. Unlike `multiplicity` and `leadingEnergy`, which get `_zero`, `_cons` and `_add`, it has no lemma for the empty state or for the operations in scope (`::ₘ`, `+`), although roadmap §0.1 explicitly asks for the behaviour of the invariant mass squared under multiset union.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:186-193 (`IsCollinearSafe.map`, `.prodMk`) and 214-221 (`IsInfraredSafe.map`, `.prodMk`) vs. 250-303, where only `IsIRCSafe` gets the algebra.
findings.fix: Add `IsCollinearSafe.map₂`/`.add`/`.neg`/`.sub`/`.mul` (hypotheses `[Add X]` etc., no `TopologicalSpace`/`Continuous*`) and the `IsInfraredSafe` counterparts, and derive the existing `IsIRCSafe.*` from the two halves.
findings.issue: `map₂`, `add`, `neg`, `sub`, `mul`, `isIRCSafe_finsetSum`, `isIRCSafe_finsetProd` exist only for `IsIRCSafe`, although the file develops `map`/`prodMk` on both `IsCollinearSafe` and `IsInfraredSafe` separately, and the roadmap reasons about the two properties separately (Layer 2.4 splits collinear and infrared safety of jet observables; Counterexamples.lean proves one-sided failures). Collinear safety of a sum/product needs no topology at all, so the IRC-only form is strictly weaker than what holds.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Data/Finset/Lattice/Fold.lean:99-100 `@[to_dual (attr := simp) le_inf_iff] protected theorem sup_le_iff {a : α} : s.sup f ≤ a ↔ ∀ b ∈ s, f b ≤ a`; `leadingEnergy_nonneg` and `le_leadingEnergy` (Counterexamples.lean:111,114) are both derived from it.
findings.issue: `leadingEnergy_le_iff` is the universal property (least upper bound) characterising `leadingEnergy` — the sole route to any inequality about it, since the body is unexposed — but it is not `@[simp]`, while its Mathlib analogue is.

summary: The surface is minimal and bodies are correctly left unexposed, but the characteristic API is incomplete: `IsCollinearSafe` has no definitional intro/elim restatement while `IsInfraredSafe` does, `invariantMassSq` has nothing beyond its `_def`, the closure lemmas exist only on `IsIRCSafe` though the file develops both one-sided predicates, and the least-upper-bound lemma for `leadingEnergy` is missing `@[simp]`.
